answer: One identity may run one bridge toll booth by locking an 80-credit bond. A spiral dial advances once per crossing and cannot run backward, and receipts bear a saffron seal bound to the booth key. It remits crossings times the toll. Auditors recompute remittance from the dial and receipts; a shortfall, reused seal, or lagging dial burns the bond. The k-th booth pays 31+8(k-1) credits, so the 1000th pays 8023 and 1000 fake booths pay 4027000 plus 80000 locked. A rented-booth ring fails: one dial cannot back many booths. Honest operators pay 31 once and recover the bond after a clean epoch.
